name: 21651-mixedprompt-8b-1gpu
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct -- an ungated mirror of the licence-gated meta-llama repo for the same weights.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
load_profile: poisson (open loop), rate = 12 req/s, no warmup, no cooldown, bounded at 1000 requests with a 1800 s safety cap.
workload: GuideLLM `synthetic_text`, single turn, bimodal: 900 rows of 50 prompt tokens and 100 rows carrying a 15000-token prefix drawn from a pool of 100, 256 output tokens on every row. Bucket weights 9:1 over 1000 requests; `request_format: plain`, no chat template; prefix caching off, so every long draw is a full prefill.
purpose: An eight-billion-parameter assistant answering mostly short questions plus occasional long-document queries at 12 requests per second on one GPU.
launch:
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# The workload's worst case is a ~15100-token prompt plus 256 output tokens.
max-model-len: 32768

# PINNED, not defaults written down: an engine built in-process is in neither per-usage-context
# default table at this commit and falls through to the library defaults of 2048 / 128, which is a
# different setup. 8192 / 1024 is what `vllm serve` picks on a >=70 GiB non-A100 card here.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# FORCED OFF, AND LOAD-BEARING. The long prompts are drawn with replacement from a pool of 100
# synthetic 15000-token prefixes, so with caching on (the V1 default) a repeated draw would skip
# the long prefill entirely and the workload would stop being the declared one.
enable-prefix-caching: false

enable-chunked-prefill: true
scheduling-policy: fcfs
long-prefill-token-threshold: 1000
